newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Thailand see border dispute solved soon.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Thailand see border dispute solved soon.

text.p: Malaysia and Thailand agreed on Thursday that a 15-year-old border demarcation dispute should be resolved within the next two months, Malaysia's Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said.
He said Thai Prime Minister General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh agreed on two principles to solve the problem during two hours of talks with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.

"The first (principle) is to establish a permanent border which will not be changed due to the shifting nature of the geographical location of a river because of floods," Abdullah told reporters after the two prime ministers met.
The second principle is to take a joint development approach so disputed areas along the border would be developed for mutual benefit, Abdullah said.
The demarcation problem arose mainly because both countries used rivers as border marks, which posed a problem because they changed as a result of flooding.
"Within 60 days, we'll be having a permanent border and we won't be bothered later on because the rivers begin to shift," Abdullah said.
Ties were ruffled last year when Malaysia began building a three-metre (10 ft) high wall topped with barbed wire along the border to stem a flow of smuggled goods and illegal immigrants.
Chavalit arrived in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday for a two-day visit, his first since becoming prime minister late last year.
